headline: A 2018 federal law lets terminally ill patients who have run out of approved treatments seek certain unapproved experimental drugs outside formal clinical trials.
what_it_does: The law exempts certain unapproved, investigational drugs from some federal rules when they are given to a terminally ill patient. The patient must have exhausted approved treatment options and be unable to join a clinical trial for the drug. Drug makers must report yearly to the Food and Drug Administration on how the drug was used, and the FDA posts a yearly summary on its website. The law also limits legal liability for drug sponsors, makers, prescribers, and dispensers who provide or decline to provide the drug under these rules.

who_it_affects.how: Those who have used all approved treatment options and cannot join a clinical trial may be able to obtain eligible unapproved investigational drugs.
They may prescribe eligible investigational drugs to qualifying patients under the law's conditions and have limited liability for doing so.
They may provide eligible investigational drugs outside standard approval requirements, must report annual use to the FDA, and have limited liability.
They may dispense eligible investigational drugs under the law and have limited liability for doing so.

when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on May 30, 2018, and took effect on that date.
